title: Mara and the Wolf
premise: Mara Vale, a charm-seller scraping by in the magic-outlawed city of Corvane, is handed a living map by a dying stranger and bound to it by blood. The map leads her to Bram Hartwell, a disgraced cartographer who once charted the Hollow King's realm, where a wolf-spirit wears the crown and devours the true king's memory one year at a time. Hunted by the king's wardens and betrayed by allies who want the map for themselves, Mara must choose between destroying the wolf — which would kill the innocent man beneath it — and finding a third path no law allows. In the end she unbinds the king not with power but by giving the wolf what it truly starves for: a place to belong, and she pays for that mercy with her own name written into the map.
about_author: Coral Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing impossible maps before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal cottage where, she insists, the tide comes in on schedule and nothing else does.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In Corvane, where magic is outlawed, Mara sells harmless trinkets disguised as charms to desperate buyers. Establishes her loneliness, her sharp survival instincts, and the warden raids that keep everyone afraid. Emotional beat: weary self-containment; she trusts no one, including herself.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses in her shop, presses a folded map into her hands, and dies whispering 'the wolf remembers.' Wardens arrive; Mara flees with the map, which moves under her fingers like skin. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Ink That Breathes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hiding in the sewers, Mara discovers the map redraws itself, showing roads that don't exist and a crowned figure at its center. Touching it pulls her through. Emotional beat: vertigo and wonder as her careful, small life ends.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram Hartwell, exiled for mapping forbidden realms, finds Mara unconscious at the edge of the Hollow King's forest. He recognizes the map he drew three years ago and the debt he owes its previous bearer. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Rules of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram teaches Mara the forest's laws: never give your true name, never eat what's offered, never look at the moon twice. They reach a village of people erased from records. Emotional beat: wary partnership forming between two people used to being alone.

chapters.title: The Village Without Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The villagers traded their names for safety long ago; now they cannot leave or die. An old woman recognizes the map and begs Mara to burn it. Emotional beat: first glimpse of the price of survival — belonging bought with erasure.

chapters.title: Wardens Cross Over
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Warden-Captain Sera Ilvane, who exiled Bram, has followed them through. She believes destroying the map will seal the breach forever, even if it kills the trapped king. Emotional beat: dread; the law has teeth even here.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. From a ridge they see the capital: a city of silver antlers where the wolf-king holds court, beautiful and wrong. Mara feels the map pulling toward him like a hook in her chest. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Bargain Market
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To enter the city they need masks woven from true names. Mara trades a memory of her mother to a broker called the Tallyman. Emotional beat: grief as currency; she learns exactly what survival costs.

chapters.title: Court of Antlers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Disguised, they attend the wolf-king's court. The king is courteous, melancholy, and occasionally flickers — a man surfacing inside the beast. He notices Mara's map and invites her to stay. Emotional beat: seduction of power and pity entwined.

chapters.title: The Man Beneath
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A servant smuggles Mara to the king's forgotten chambers, where she meets Aldric, the true king's remnant, kept like a pressed flower. He asks her not to save him — only to remember him. Emotional beat: compassion against pragmatism.

chapters.title: Sera's Verdict
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera captures Bram and offers Mara amnesty if she surrenders the map. Flashbacks reveal Sera once loved someone consumed by the Hollow and will burn anything to end it. Emotional beat: righteous certainty cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bridge
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara trades the map to Sera to free Bram — then discovers the Tallyman sold her location to the wolf-king. The bridge burns behind them. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal; trust becomes a luxury.

chapters.title: Wolf at the Door
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The wolf-king corners them, not to kill but to bargain: return his map, and he'll let the villages go. Bram realizes the wolf isn't a conqueror — it's a guardian that ate a crown to keep the realm from collapsing. Emotional beat: moral ground shifting.

chapters.title: The Map's First Owner
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The dying stranger's past unfolds through the map's ink: he was the first cartographer, who bound the wolf to the king to imprison both. Every 'rescue' since has fed the cage. Emotional beat: fury at the architects of suffering.

chapters.title: Allies of Necessity
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Mara, Bram, a defected Sera, and the nameless villagers gather in the forest. Their plan: not to kill the wolf or free the king, but to rewrite the binding — a map drawn by many hands. Emotional beat: fragile, hard-won solidarity.

chapters.title: The Tallyman's Price
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. To draw a new binding, Mara needs back what she sold. The Tallyman agrees — for her future, every year she hasn't lived yet. She signs. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely at last, not forced.

chapters.title: Storming the Silver Court
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The assault on the capital: villagers without names slip past wards that hunt identities, while Sera holds the gates. Bram reaches the throne room and begins drawing over the old lines in live ink. Emotional beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax. The wolf fights the redrawing; Aldric's remnant chooses to stand with the beast rather than be freed alone. Mara offers the wolf the thing no one ever did: a name of its own, and a place beside the king instead of beneath the crown. Emotional beat: mercy as the sharpest blade.

chapters.title: Two Kings, One Crown
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The binding rewrites: wolf and king share the crown as co-sovereigns, the Hollow stabilizing around shared rule rather than consumption. Sera stands down, her warrant meaningless against a new law. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving hope.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Resolution begins. Mara's stolen years manifest — her hair silvered, her memories thinning at the edges. Bram refuses to let her fade unnamed and writes her story onto the map so the realm itself will hold her. Emotional beat: tenderness against loss.

chapters.title: Mara and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Epilogue. Mara stays in the Hollow as its cartographer, mapping a realm that finally belongs to itself; the wolf walks beside her, named and home. Her old life is gone, but for the first time she belongs somewhere. Final beat: bittersweet peace — survival's price paid, justice found outside any law.
